title: Subscription Total Kept Fee And Credit As Separate Signs
text: id: COMP-012 domain: math title: Subscription Total Kept Fee And Credit As Separate Signs tags: money, subscription, credit memory: A subscription total once drifted because I treated a credit like another fee. I wrote monthly cost times months, then setup fee as a plus, then credit as a minus. Seeing the signs separately kept the final price honest. The bill matched when the credit stayed negative.

title: Tiered Pricing Split Base Units Extra Units Fixed Fee
text: id: COMP-001 domain: math title: Tiered Pricing Split Base Units Extra Units Fixed Fee tags: tiered-pricing, units, addition memory: I once answered a tiered utility bill too quickly and charged every unit at the blended-looking rate. The correction was embarrassing because the structure was simple: first tier, extra units, fixed fee. I rewrote it as 100 base units, then units above 100, then the fixed charge. The revised bill matched the invoice exactly, and I remembered how a tier problem punishes shortcuts.

title: Money Problems Kept Cents To Two Decimal Places
text: id: COMP-019 domain: math title: Money Problems Kept Cents To Two Decimal Places tags: money, rounding, decimals memory: A money answer once looked close but failed because I rounded too early. I kept cents through the calculation and rounded only at the final bill. The tax, fee, credit, and tier amounts each got two decimal places. The final dollar amount became both readable and exact enough.
